values.note: $20 a night, with the fee and registration procedure posted at the campground kiosk. A Recreation Passport is required for vehicle entry to every state forest campground.

fees.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/forks ('Overnight fees ($20 for most sites) and registration procedures are posted at the information kiosk at each campground'; 'A Recreation Passport (park pass) is required for vehicle entry into all state park and forest campgrounds') + https://www.michigan.gov/dnr/things-to-do/camping-and-lodging/state-forest-campgrounds/amenity-table (Forks State Forest Campground: 9 sites, $20), read 2026-10-25

values.note: Drinking water from a hand-pump well. Carry-in access to the Boardman River; the campground is also reachable by canoe from the river. No boat ramp.

facilities.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/forks ('There are vault toilets.' 'Potable (drinking) water is available from a hand-pump well.' 'This campground is accessible from the Boardman River for canoe camping.') + amenity table (boat access: C), read 2026-10-25

booking.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/forks ('No reservations. Sites available on a first-come, first-served basis.' 'Camping is limited to a 15-day maximum stay.') + amenity table ('Reservable at MiDNRReservations.com': no), read 2026-10-25

values.note: 'Nine rustic sites suitable for tents and small trailers' (the DNR's standard state forest wording; no maximum length posted). One camping unit and six people per site.

sites.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/forks ('With nine rustic sites suitable for tents and small trailers'; 'One camping unit and six people are allowed per site') + amenity table (9 campsites), read 2026-10-25

note: Rustic Michigan DNR state forest campground in pines and hardwoods on the Boardman River (Blue Ribbon trout stream, Natural River), 8585 Brown Bridge Road, 7 miles south of Williamsburg via Williamsburg, Supply and Brown Bridge roads, Grand Traverse County; managed by Traverse City State Park. ORV trails nearby (the DNR table does not allow riding between the campground and the trails). --Claude
summary: DNR page + SF amenity table: 9 sites, $20 at the kiosk + Recreation Passport, no electric, vault toilets, hand-pump water, carry-in/paddle-in river access, first-come only, 15-day max (all confirmed; the 15-night max had been inherited). Season (open all year, roads not plowed) already manual and matches. Phone 231-922-5270 matches (Traverse City SP). Note trimmed of field restatements.
